entries.title: Imaging Modality Principles (X-Ray/Fluoroscopy, Computed Tomography, Ultrasound, MRI, PET-CT): Physics, Indications, and Relative Radiation Exposure

testable_competencies.classification: Classify the basic physics, general indications, and relative radiation exposure of the major imaging modalities (x-ray/fluoroscopy, CT, ultrasound, MRI, PET) as background for modality-selection decisions made within every organ-system unit later in the chapter.

entries.zero_question_reason: Foundational modality-physics background (attenuation, Hounsfield units, echogenicity, T1/T2 relaxation), not independently testable at the MCCQE level; frames the presentation-specific modality-selection competencies tested in every subsequent unit.

entries.title: Contrast Agents and Contrast Safety (Iodinated Contrast, Gadolinium, Barium, Microbubbles; Contrast-Induced Nephropathy Prevention)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 89-2's scope of diagnosing/managing the complications of CKD encompasses recognizing contrast-induced nephropathy risk and applying preventive measures in patients with reduced renal function; contrast safety itself is not separately named in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.safety: Recognize contraindications to IV/oral/rectal contrast agents (prior adverse reaction, renal impairment, dehydration, myasthenia gravis, right-to-left cardiac shunt for microbubbles) and appropriate preventive hydration strategies before contrast-enhanced imaging in at-risk patients.

entries.title: Chest X-Ray Views and Chest CT Approach (Technique, Systematic Interpretation, Windowing)

testable_competencies.classification: Recognize the general purpose of standard CXR views (PA, lateral, AP, decubitus, lordotic) and CT windowing (soft tissue/bone/lung) as background for interpreting the specific chest findings tested in SU-MI-04 through SU-MI-09.

entries.zero_question_reason: Systematic film-reading technique (the ABCDEF mnemonic, windowing) is an interpretive radiology skill beyond graduating-student scope per project instructions; the clinically actionable content (recognizing specific abnormalities) is scoped separately.

entries.title: Recognition of Airspace and Parenchymal Lung Abnormalities (Atelectasis, Consolidation/Pneumonia, Pulmonary Nodule)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 27's diagnostic approach to dyspnea encompasses recognizing consolidation/pneumonia and atelectasis on chest imaging as causes of respiratory symptoms, though these findings are not individually named in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize atelectasis and consolidation on CXR (silhouette sign, air bronchograms) and correlate with the likely underlying pneumonia or obstructive etiology.
testable_competencies.management: Determine when a solitary pulmonary nodule requires further imaging (CT, PET/CT) versus Fleischner-guideline follow-up based on malignancy-risk features.

entries.title: Interstitial Lung Disease Imaging Patterns

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize a reticulonodular/interstitial imaging pattern as suggestive of interstitial lung disease requiring pulmonology referral, without needing to distinguish the full occupational/autoimmune/drug-related differential.

entries.zero_question_reason: No MCC objective addresses interstitial lung disease imaging specifically; the extensive occupational/autoimmune/drug-related/idiopathic differential (FASSTEN, BAD RASH mnemonics) exceeds graduating-student scope and is appropriately treated as specialist detail per project instructions to avoid detailed specialist-only image-pattern trivia.

entries.title: Pulmonary Vascular Abnormalities: Pulmonary Edema and Pulmonary Embolism Imaging

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 27 explicitly requires identifying life-threatening causes of dyspnea; pulmonary embolism and cardiogenic pulmonary edema are the paradigmatic life-threatening/high-yield causes for which this unit's imaging-selection competency (CT pulmonary angiography vs. V/Q scan) directly supports the objective's diagnostic-approach requirement.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: PE is a life-threatening cause of chest pain that objective 14 requires excluding; this unit's imaging-selection competency supports that diagnostic pathway.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Select CT pulmonary angiography as the definitive imaging study for suspected pulmonary embolism, and recognize V/Q scan as the preferred alternative in patients with renal impairment or in pregnancy.
testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize the CXR and CT findings of pulmonary edema and their correlation with cardiogenic vs. non-cardiogenic etiology.

entries.title: Pleural Abnormalities (Pleural Effusion, Pneumothorax including Tension Pneumothorax, Asbestos-Related Disease)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This is a near-exact, named-title match: objective 76 is scoped precisely to pleural effusion, and this unit's imaging-recognition competency (view sensitivity, U/S superiority for small effusions) directly supports the objective's diagnostic approach.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Tension pneumothorax is a life-threatening cause of dyspnea that objective 27 explicitly requires identifying; this unit's imaging-recognition competency directly supports that requirement.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize pneumothorax (including tension pneumothorax with mediastinal shift) on upright and supine chest imaging, and recognize pleural effusion, including which plain-film view is most sensitive for small effusions.
testable_competencies.management: Recognize the urgent management implications of tension pneumothorax identified on imaging (needle decompression, chest tube).

entries.title: Mediastinal Abnormalities and Cardiac Silhouette (Mediastinal Mass Compartments, Cardiomegaly)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This is a near-exact, named-title match: objective 54-1 explicitly requires differentiating causes of mediastinal mass based on radiographic compartment location, which is precisely this unit's core competency (Felson's method, 4Ts mnemonic).

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Localize a mediastinal mass to the anterior, middle, or posterior compartment using Felson's method and generate an appropriate differential diagnosis for each compartment.
testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize cardiomegaly on chest imaging using the cardiothoracic ratio.

entries.title: Tubes, Lines, and Catheters: Recognizing Position and Complications on Chest Imaging

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize grossly malpositioned central lines, endotracheal tubes, or chest tubes on CXR as a patient-safety check, without needing precise millimeter-level positioning criteria.

entries.zero_question_reason: No MCC objective addresses line/tube positioning specifically; the precise positioning criteria (e.g., exact centimeter tip locations) are ICU/postoperative radiology-specialist detail exceeding graduating-student scope.

entries.title: Abdominal X-Ray Indications and Systematic Approach (Free ABDO, Bowel Gas Patterns, Volvulus, Obstruction)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-2 explicitly requires identifying patients requiring emergency medical or surgical treatment for acute abdominal pain; free air, bowel obstruction, and volvulus are the paradigmatic emergent AXR findings this unit's recognition competency supports.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 1 explicitly requires differentiating ascites from bowel obstruction, matching this unit's AXR bowel-gas-pattern and free-fluid recognition competency directly.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize free intraperitoneal air, bowel obstruction (small vs. large bowel dilation using the 3-6-9 rule), and volvulus patterns on AXR as indications for urgent surgical consultation.

entries.title: Abdominal CT Approach, Contrast Studies, and Bowel Obstruction/CT Colonography

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: CT is the modality of choice for determining the cause of bowel obstruction per objective 3-2's diagnostic-approach scope, though the specific CT-technique/contrast-route content is not itself named in the retrieved excerpt.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: CT colonography is one accepted modality for colorectal cancer screening/surveillance, loosely relevant to objective 6-2's screening-risk-identification component, but is not itself named in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Select appropriate contrast route (IV, oral, rectal) for abdominal CT based on clinical indication, and apply the 3-6-9 rule to identify bowel obstruction on CT.

entries.title: Specific Visceral Organ Imaging (Liver, Spleen, Biliary Tree: Modality Selection and Mass Characterization)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 2's requirement to order pertinent investigations to determine the most likely diagnosis for an abdominal mass encompasses selecting U/S, CT, or MRI to characterize a liver mass, though liver-specific imaging is not itself named in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Select the appropriate follow-up imaging modality (CT or MRI) after an incidental liver lesion is identified on ultrasound, and recognize cirrhosis findings across modalities.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantially overlaps Gastroenterology (G, completed) liver-mass/cirrhosis content; this unit is scoped to imaging-modality selection only, not hepatology management.

entries.title: Acute Abdominal "-itis" Imaging: Best Initial Modality for Cholecystitis, Appendicitis, Diverticulitis, and Pancreatitis

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 3-2's key objective to diagnose the cause of acute abdominal pain and identify patients requiring emergency treatment directly matches this unit's core competency: selecting U/S for suspected acute cholecystitis, U/S or CT for appendicitis, and CT for diverticulitis and pancreatitis.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Select the best initial imaging modality for suspected acute cholecystitis (U/S), acute appendicitis (U/S or CT depending on age/habitus), acute diverticulitis (CT), and acute pancreatitis (U/S for screening, CT for complications).

entries.title: Angiography of the Gastrointestinal Tract (GI Bleed Localization)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 6-1's management-plan scope for GI bleeding includes angiographic localization/embolization when endoscopic therapy fails or is unavailable, though angiography is not itself named in the retrieved excerpt.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: CT angiography is a first-line localization tool for active lower GI bleeding, matching objective 6-2's diagnostic-approach scope.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize CT angiography as the modality of choice for localizing an active GI bleed, given active bleeding at a sufficient rate is required for angiographic visualization.

entries.title: Urological Imaging (KUB, Renal Colic and Renal Mass CT incl. Bosniak Classification, Retrograde Studies, Renal Nuclear Scan)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 8 requires diagnosing the cause of hematuria; CT urography (high sensitivity for uroepithelial malignancy) and triphasic CT (for renal mass characterization, Bosniak classification) are the primary imaging tools supporting this diagnostic pathway.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Renal nuclear scans and modality choice are influenced by renal function, a loose secondary link to objective 89-2's CKD scope rather than a direct match.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Select the appropriate initial imaging modality for suspected renal colic (CT KUB) and for hematuria/suspected renal mass (CT urography, triphasic CT), and apply the Bosniak classification to determine whether a cystic renal mass requires follow-up or urological referral.

entries.title: Gynecological Imaging (Transabdominal/Transvaginal Ultrasound, Hysterosalpingogram, Sonohysterogram)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Transvaginal ultrasound is the primary imaging tool for evaluating suspected ectopic pregnancy and early pregnancy loss, within objective 81's diagnostic scope, though TVUS is not itself named in the retrieved excerpt.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Hysterosalpingogram (HSG) is a named investigation for tubal-patency assessment in the infertility workup, matching objective 46's diagnostic scope.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Select transvaginal ultrasound as first-line imaging for suspected ectopic pregnancy or early pregnancy complications, and recognize hysterosalpingogram as the investigation of choice for tubal-patency assessment in infertility workup.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantially overlaps Gynecology (GY, completed); this unit is scoped to imaging-modality selection only, not gynecological disease management.

entries.title: Adrenal Mass Imaging Characterization

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize an adrenal 'incidentaloma' identified on CT and the general concept that CT/MRI features help distinguish benign adenoma from carcinoma or pheochromocytoma, without needing precise Hounsfield-unit washout thresholds.

entries.zero_question_reason: No MCC objective addresses adrenal mass imaging specifically; the detailed CT/MRI washout and enhancement thresholds distinguishing adenoma from carcinoma/pheochromocytoma/metastasis are specialist-level detail exceeding graduating-student scope.

entries.title: Approach to Head Computed Tomography and Modality Selection by Neurologic Presentation

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 109-10 explicitly requires determining appropriate imaging for traumatic brain injury; CT as the first-line modality for acute craniofacial trauma and the 'danger signs' checklist directly support this requirement.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Head CT is the primary initial imaging investigation for altered mental status/coma of unclear etiology, matching objective 58-1's diagnostic-approach scope.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Select CT as the first-line imaging modality for acute head trauma, suspected intracranial hemorrhage, altered mental status, and hydrocephalus, and recognize danger signs on head CT (mass effect, midline shift, herniation) requiring urgent neurosurgical consultation.

entries.title: Cerebrovascular Disease and Stroke Imaging (CT vs. MRI Timing, Carotid/Cerebral Angiography)

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Cerebrovascular accident and transient ischemic attack (stroke)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This is a near-exact, named-title match: objective 41's diagnostic-approach requirement for stroke depends directly on this unit's core competency of selecting CT (initial, to exclude hemorrhage and determine thrombolysis/thrombectomy eligibility) versus MRI (more sensitive for early ischemia).

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Select non-contrast CT as the initial imaging study in suspected acute stroke to exclude hemorrhage and guide time-sensitive thrombolysis/thrombectomy decisions, recognizing MRI's greater sensitivity for early ischemic change when the diagnosis remains unclear.

entries.title: CNS Infection and Demyelinating Disease Imaging (Meningitis/Encephalitis/Cerebral Abscess, Multiple Sclerosis)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 107-1's key objective to rule out life-threatening causes of fever (e.g. meningococcal meningitis) is supported by this unit's imaging-recognition competency (MRI meningeal enhancement), though a normal MRI does not rule out leptomeningitis and imaging must not delay treatment.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize that MRI, not CT, is the preferred modality for suspected CNS infection or demyelinating disease, while understanding that a normal MRI does not exclude meningitis and must never delay empiric antibiotics.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantially overlaps Infectious Diseases (SU-ID-09, completed) and Neurology (N, not yet mapped); this unit is scoped to imaging-modality selection and radiographic pattern recognition only.

entries.title: Musculoskeletal Imaging Modality Selection, Approach to Bone X-Ray, and Fracture Description

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 109-3 requires diagnosing and assessing severity of a bone or joint injury; this unit's plain-film-first imaging approach (orthogonal views, joint above/below imaging) and fracture-description terminology directly support that diagnostic process.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Select plain film as the initial study for suspected fracture/dislocation, obtaining orthogonal views and imaging the joint above and below the injury, and recognize when CT is indicated for occult or complex intra-articular fractures.

entries.title: Arthritis Imaging (Cross-Reference to Rheumatology)

testable_competencies.cross_reference: Recognize that radiographic features of specific arthritides are covered under Rheumatology, not as independent MI-chapter content.

entries.zero_question_reason: Body-confirmed as a pure cross-reference to Rheumatology; no independent clinical content exists in this chapter.
entries.cross_discipline_note: Cross-references Rheumatology (RH, not yet mapped) for the actual radiographic-arthritis content.

entries.title: Bone and Soft Tissue Tumours: Aggressive vs. Non-Aggressive Lesion Recognition

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 53 explicitly requires distinguishing benign from malignant musculoskeletal lumps/masses; this unit's aggressive-vs-non-aggressive imaging feature recognition (zone of transition, periosteal reaction, cortical destruction) is the primary tool supporting that distinction.

testable_competencies.recognition: Distinguish aggressive from non-aggressive bone lesions on x-ray using periosteal reaction pattern (Codman's triangle/onion skin/sunburst vs. benign remodeling), zone of transition, and presence of a soft tissue mass, to determine urgency of biopsy/referral.

entries.title: Musculoskeletal Infection Imaging (Osteomyelitis, Septic Arthritis, Necrotizing Fasciitis)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 50-3's causal_conditions explicitly names osteomyelitis and necrotizing fasciitis under infectious causes of acute localized musculoskeletal pain, matching this unit's imaging-recognition competency for these surgical/medical emergencies directly.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Oligoarthralgia (pain in one to four joints)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 50-1's causal_conditions names infection under acute joint pain; this unit's key teaching point that imaging cannot rule out septic arthritis and aspiration is required regardless directly supports the objective's urgency-recognition requirement.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize that plain films are frequently normal early in septic arthritis and necrotizing fasciitis, and that a normal or unremarkable x-ray must never delay joint aspiration or surgical exploration when clinical suspicion is high; recognize MRI as the most sensitive modality for osteomyelitis.

entries.title: Metabolic Bone Disease Imaging (Osteoporosis/DEXA, Osteomalacia, Hyperparathyroidism, Paget's Disease)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Age/sex-specific screening for osteoporosis via DEXA is a named preventive-health-advice component under objective 74's scope; hyperparathyroidism/Paget's-specific imaging findings are not themselves named in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.screening: Recognize DEXA as the gold-standard screening/diagnostic tool for osteoporosis and interpret T-score thresholds for osteopenia and osteoporosis.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantially overlaps Endocrinology (E, completed - osteoporosis E46, Paget's E50); this unit is scoped to imaging/screening-modality selection only.

entries.title: Nuclear Medicine Brain Imaging (SPECT/PET for Dementia, Traumatic Brain Injury, Seizure Focus Localization)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: FDG-PET's role in differentiating dementia subtypes is a diagnostic-approach adjunct within objective 58-3's scope, though PET imaging is not itself named in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize that SPECT/PET brain imaging has a role as an adjunct in atypical dementia workup and epileptic-focus localization, without needing specific radiotracer uptake-pattern detail.

entries.title: Nuclear Medicine Thyroid Imaging (Radioactive Iodine Uptake, Scintiscan Hot/Cold Nodules, Radioiodine Ablation)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 63 requires excluding malignancy in a patient with a thyroid nodule; hot vs. cold nodule classification on scintiscan is a key diagnostic tool directly supporting this requirement (cold nodules require biopsy exclusion of malignancy).

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Interpret RAIU as elevated in hyperthyroid states with increased thyroid synthesis (Graves', toxic multinodular goitre) versus decreased in thyroiditis or exogenous hormone use, and recognize that a 'cold' nodule on thyroid scintiscan requires biopsy to exclude malignancy while a 'hot' nodule is reassuring.

entries.title: Nuclear Medicine Respiratory and Cardiac Imaging (V/Q Scan including Pregnancy Considerations, Myocardial Perfusion Scan, MUGA)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: V/Q scan is an accepted alternative to CT pulmonary angiography for ruling out PE in objective 27's dyspnea diagnostic pathway, with specific relevance in pregnancy (lower fetal radiation dose) and renal impairment.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize V/Q scan (or a modified perfusion-only, lower-dose protocol) as the preferred pulmonary embolism imaging strategy in pregnant patients with a normal CXR.
testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize the general concept of myocardial perfusion scanning to distinguish reversible ischemia from fixed infarction.

entries.title: Nuclear Medicine Abdominal and Genitourinary Imaging (HIDA Scan, RBC Scan for GI Bleed, Urea Breath Test, Functional Renal Imaging)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Tagged RBC scan is used for slow-rate GI bleed localization when angiography is not diagnostic, a loose secondary link to objective 6-1's management-plan scope rather than a direct named match.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize HIDA scan as the confirmatory study for acute cholecystitis when abdominal ultrasound is equivocal, and the urea breath test as the preferred non-invasive method to diagnose and confirm eradication of active H. pylori infection.

entries.title: Interventional Radiology Vascular Procedures (Angiography, Angioplasty/Stents, Thrombolysis, Embolization, IVC Filter, Central Venous Access)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Endovascular repair/embolization is one management option within objective 109-15's revascularization scope, but the specific IR-procedural techniques and device selection are not named in the retrieved excerpt and exceed the objective's generalist framing.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: IVC filter is one option for VTE-recurrence prevention when anticoagulation is contraindicated, a loose secondary link to this objective's scope rather than a direct match.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize the general indications for referral to interventional radiology (angioplasty/stenting for vascular stenosis, thrombolysis for acute limb ischemia or PE, embolization for uncontrolled hemorrhage, IVC filter when anticoagulation is contraindicated), without needing specific procedural technique detail.

entries.title: Breast Imaging Modality Selection by Age and Presentation (Mammography, Ultrasound, MRI, BI-RADS)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 10-1 requires diagnosing the cause of a breast mass and recommending appropriate screening; this unit's age-based modality-selection competency (U/S first-line under 30 and in pregnancy/lactation, mammography over 30, BI-RADS-driven follow-up) directly supports both the diagnostic and screening components.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Mammography/U/S workup of nipple discharge is part of objective 10-2's diagnostic scope, though not itself individually named in the retrieved excerpt.

entries.title: Breast Diagnostic/Interventional Procedures and Mammographic Feature Characterization (Benign vs. Malignant Masses)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Distinguishing benign from malignant mammographic features (shape, margin, calcification pattern) is a diagnostic-approach component of objective 10-1's scope, though these specific radiographic features are not individually named in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.recognition: Distinguish benign (circumscribed, oval, popcorn calcification) from malignant (irregular, spiculated, pleomorphic calcification) mammographic mass features, and recognize when core needle biopsy is indicated for a BI-RADS 4/5 finding.

entries.title: Landmark Radiology Trials and Chapter References

testable_competencies.reference: Recognize landmark radiology trial concepts (e.g., IVC filter risk/benefit, endovascular vs. open AAA repair, contrast-nephropathy hydration prophylaxis) as background reference material; specific trial statistics are not independently testable at the scope layer.

entries.zero_question_reason: Pure landmark-trial summary table and chapter bibliography; per project instructions, trial-level statistics are not encoded into the scope layer. Clinical conclusions relevant to specific units (e.g., contrast-nephropathy prophylaxis for SU-MI-02, IVC filter for SU-MI-30) will be researched from current guidance during question generation.
